chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr al-Bazanṭī narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who vowed upon himself that, if he recovered from an illness or was released from imprisonment, he would fast every Wednesday, and it was the day on which he was released. Then he became unable to do that because of an ailment that afflicted him or something else, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prolonged the man’s life, so many fasts accumulated upon him. What is the expiation for that? He said: “He should give charity for each day, a mudd of wheat or a mudd of dates.”

key_terms.مُدًّا: a mudd, a standard measure of food
key_terms.نَذَرَ: made a vow binding upon himself

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for missed fasts from a vow that a person was unable to fulfill?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a vowed fast that a person later becomes unable to fulfill. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that when many such missed fasts accumulate due to inability, the expiation is to give charity for each missed day, consisting of a mudd of wheat or a mudd of dates.
